original.title: Discipline and Punish: The Birth of the Prison
original.note: Book checked in Open Library (/works/OL26841W, first published 1975). ISBN is one edition's; cite the edition you read.

core_idea: Power is not only held and imposed from above. It works through knowledge, norms and everyday practices that discipline bodies and shape what counts as normal. Discourses define what can be said, by whom and with what authority.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do institutions such as schools, hospitals or prisons regulate people?
How does a discourse construct a group (e.g. migrants, 'at-risk' youth)?
Typical data: archival and document analysis, genealogy, discourse analysis.
common_mistakes: Citing Foucault without a method (genealogy, archaeology).
Treating power as purely repressive, which Foucault rejects.
